flags.title: A 'from' price and a parcel weight are the two things a scraped listing gets wrong loudest
flags.finding: Two traps this pass caught before they reached the table. (1) Product-level minimums: Automic Gold's Leaves Signet Ring lists 'from $2,194' on a page whose options run to $2,744 (Salt & Pepper lab diamond) and $3,068 (platinum), and its Cluster Signet Ring's 'from $1,636' is one of several option prices; both rows were confirmed against the exact option combination (14k Yellow Gold / Clear Lab Diamond = 2194.00; 14k Yellow Gold / Lab Diamond = 1636.00) instead of the headline. The same effect explains every apparent 'drift' in an earlier automated sweep except the two Menē rows: the reader was comparing a karat-specific stored price with a product-wide minimum. (2) Parcel weight: Ross-Simons's variant records publish "grams":113 on every size of every product, from an $89 ring to a $695 ring - it is the shipping weight (0.25 lb), 113 g is 0.25 lb - the shipping weight of the box - and a 113 g gold band would be an entirely different product from anything on this page.
flags.what_is_missing: Nothing in the dataset - recorded so that the next pass, or a reader reusing the raw capture, does not read a product-level minimum as a karat's price or a parcel weight as gold content.
flags.why_it_matters: Both mistakes inflate or deflate a ring's apparent value by an order of magnitude, and both look like clean machine-readable numbers, which is exactly how a hallucinated price gets into a table of verified prices.
flags.buyer_action: When you check a price, select the metal and stone you intend to buy and read the number under the selection - never the 'from' figure on the card.

flags.finding: Auvere's 22K pages publish size-dependent gram ranges labelled 'Approximate Fine Weight : X to Y grams depending on size' together with the sentence 'Each Auvere piece is handcrafted to order; your piece may weigh more or less than the gold weight listed', and - in the page's own JSON-LD description - a single figure for some pieces that does not agree with the range on the same page: the Small V Neck Pendant prints '2.9 to 3.7 grams' in the spec panel and 'an approximate gold weight of 2.8 g' in the description, and the Clean Cut Chain prints '2.8 to 3.7 grams' against 'an approximate gold weight of 2.7 grams'. The two 22K diamond cuffs publish a range only (bridge tall 5 to 6.1 g, hexagon 3.3 to 3.5 g) and no single figure anywhere.
flags.resolution: Left blank on purpose, again, on 2026-10-23 (ninth pass). Both statements were re-read today from the live pages and are quoted verbatim on each row; no number was averaged, and no range was stored as a single weight. A buyer who wants Auvere's own figure should read the row's note, where both the range and the single-figure sentence are recorded.

flags.finding: Six retailers refused the GitHub Actions runner's IP on 2026-10-23: With Clarity returned HTTP 403 on the product page and on its .js/.json endpoints for all five rows, and Ross-Simons, Cartier, Brilliant Earth and Menē refused their JSON endpoints outright. Ten rows returned no usable page text at all on the 20:32Z run (five With Clarity, one Brilliant Earth, two Cartier Etincelle, the 1895 band and the Destinee/Etincelle page).
flags.resolution: Resolved on the ninth pass the same way: the ten blocked rows were read on this session's own fetch channel (Cartier etincelle-emerald, Cartier destinee, Menē both bands, Brilliant Earth setting, withclarity.com/products/tulip-basket-alternating-diamond-ring-14k-yellow-gold.js) and six of them (wc-4prong, wc-4prong-petite, wc-6prong, wc-gerbera, be-18k-6p-121h6 in part) keep their earlier same-day reads, which are labelled as such on every row page and in the ledger. The two rows the ninth pass could not read on any channel are listed explicitly as not read today: see data/session-7626fc93/hand-reads-2026-10-23.json.
